reasoning_summary: If A minus B is empty, every element of A lies in B, so A is a subset of B. The complement inclusion in option 2 is reversed; union is not cancellative as in option 3; and equal set differences force A equals B, not an empty intersection, in option 4.
For an arithmetic sequence, a10 minus a6 equals 4d, so 10 minus 4 equals 4d and d equals 3/2. Then a16 equals a10 plus 6d equals 10 plus 9 equals 19.
The common difference is (a18 minus a7)/(18 minus 7) = (7 minus 18)/11 = -1. Starting from a18 = 7, seven more steps reach zero, hence a25 = 0.
Write ak = a1 + (k-1)d with d nonzero. Substitution gives 2a1 + 2(n-2)d = 2a1 + (n+5)d, so 2n - 4 = n + 5 and n = 9.
Using ak = a1 + (k-1)d, the condition a27 = 2a18 gives a1 + 26d = 2a1 + 34d, hence a1 = -8d. Therefore a9 = a1 + 8d = 0.
